headline: A new GLP-1 pill
arrives.
dek: FDA has approved orforglipron, a daily tablet that is not a peptide. Here is what the trials showed.
photoAlt: A line cook in a black work shirt holds a folded notice.
byline: Adonis Men’s Health · Checked Nov 2, 2026 · Clinical review pending

glance.label: FDA approved
glance.line: Foundayo tablets, April 1, 2026, for weight management in adults only.

glance.label: The trials
glance.line: Two 72-week placebo trials: 3,127 adults without diabetes, 1,613 with it.

glance.label: Side effects

body: On April 1, 2026, FDA approved [[/orforglipron|orforglipron]], made by Eli Lilly and sold as Foundayo, a once-daily tablet for weight management.[^nda][^fdapr] Agency records class it as a new molecular entity, a drug never approved before in any form.[^nda] It is also unusual inside its class. Most GLP-1 drugs are peptides, small proteins, usually given as weekly injections. Orforglipron is not. The researchers behind its main trial described it as “a small-molecule, nonpeptide oral glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist”.[^attain1]

It is not the first GLP-1 tablet for weight. FDA approved a tablet form of Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy, which contains [[/semaglutide|semaglutide]], on December 22, 2025.[^wegtab] What sets the new drug apart, in FDA’s words, is that it is “a GLP-1 receptor partial agonist pill which does not need to be taken on an empty stomach,”[^fdapr] according to Tracy Beth Høeg, the acting head of the agency’s drug center. The label says to take it once a day “with or without food.”[^label]

FDA decided quickly. Foundayo was the first new molecular entity approved under the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher pilot, launched in 2025.[^fdapr] FDA says it acted 50 days after filing, well ahead of a standard review deadline of January 20, 2027. “It is also the fastest approval of an NME since 2002.”[^fdapr] Lilly, for its part, said the drug would be available as early as April 6, according to Healio’s report of the company’s announcement.[^healio]

The approval rests on two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, both paid for by Lilly and both lasting 72 weeks.[^fdapr][^label] The first, ATTAIN-1, enrolled 3,127 adults with obesity, or with overweight and at least one weight-related condition such as high blood pressure or sleep apnea; people with type 2 diabetes were excluded.[^label] Their average age was 45, and 64% were women, so men were a minority.[^label] All got diet and exercise advice plus one of three daily doses or placebo. The trial used an earlier capsule form; the label translates those doses into the tablets now sold.[^label] The main measure was the percent change in body weight. Average weight fell by 7.5%, 8.4% and 11.2% on the three doses, against 2.1% on placebo.[^attain1] On the highest dose, 54.6% lost at least a tenth of their body weight, compared with 12.9% on placebo.[^attain1]

The second trial, ATTAIN-2, enrolled 1,613 adults with type 2 diabetes and a body mass index of 27 or more; their average age was 57, and 47% were women.[^label] After 72 weeks, weight fell by 5.1%, 7.0% and 9.6% on the three doses, against 2.5% on placebo.[^label] Even so, type 2 diabetes is not on the US label: Foundayo is approved for weight only, and using it to treat diabetes alone would be off-label.[^label]

The side effects are mostly digestive. In the pooled weight trials, stomach and bowel problems hit 60% to 69% of people on Foundayo, depending on dose, against 37% on placebo.[^label] Nausea, vomiting and diarrhea were most frequent while the dose was being raised, then eased.[^label] Across both trials, 8% on the drug stopped for side effects, against 3% on placebo.[^label] The label also warns of pancreatitis, kidney injury from dehydration, low blood sugar, gallbladder disease and food entering the lungs under anesthesia.[^label] It says plainly: “Concomitant use with another GLP-1 receptor agonist is not recommended.”[^label]

Like other GLP-1 drugs, Foundayo has a boxed warning, FDA’s strongest kind, about thyroid C-cell tumors. Its case differs. Other GLP-1 drugs caused these tumors in rodents, but the label says that “Orforglipron is not pharmacologically active in rats or mice and did not produce tumors in rodents”.[^label] That does not settle the question: the label still says “the human relevance of GLP-1 receptor-dependent thyroid C-cell tumors observed in rodents has not been determined”.[^label] Men with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer must not take it.[^label]

How does it compare with the injections? No trial on the label pits it against weekly [[/tirzepatide|tirzepatide]] or injected semaglutide for weight, so separate trials cannot be compared as a contest. The closest head-to-head test was in diabetes. ACHIEVE-3, an open-label Lilly trial in 1,698 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, compared orforglipron with oral semaglutide for 52 weeks. Long-term blood sugar fell more on orforglipron, but the authors reported that “the incidence of gastrointestinal events, discontinuations due to adverse events, and mean increase in pulse rate were higher with orforglipron than oral semaglutide.”[^achieve3]

Then there are the compounded versions of semaglutide and tirzepatide that spread during the shortages. FDA is direct: “Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. This means that FDA does not verify the safety, effectiveness or quality of compounded drugs before they are marketed.”[^cqa] On the day Foundayo was approved, the agency also reminded compounders that “Tirzepatide and semaglutide do not currently appear on the 503B bulks list or on FDA’s drug shortage list.”[^clarify] It warns that unapproved versions “do not undergo FDA’s review for safety, effectiveness and quality before they are marketed.”[^concerns]

Much is still unknown. The weight trials ran 72 weeks; nobody yet knows how the drug performs over many years, or what happens to weight after stopping. The one heart-safety trial so far, ACHIEVE-4, was in 2,749 adults with type 2 diabetes at high heart risk, 62.5% of them men. Over a median of two years, heart attack, stroke, heart-related death or hospital stay for unstable angina occurred in 4.2% on orforglipron and 5.0% on insulin glargine, meeting its goal of showing the drug was no worse.[^achieve4] It was a safety test against insulin, not proof that the pill protects the heart, and it did not include people without diabetes.

Next steps are mostly abroad. The UK authorised Foundayo on August 10, 2026, for both weight management and type 2 diabetes.[^mhra] In Europe, the EMA’s medicines committee adopted a positive opinion on October 15, 2026; a final decision by the European Commission is still to come.[^ema] In the US, the label covers weight alone.[^label]
